Chapter 01 of 19

The Morning Meeting

Trout Lake80 BPM
The story

Every morning, before the sun comes up, a thin mist lies on Trout Lake. It hangs in the reeds and drifts over the glassy water, so light you could walk through it and not notice. This is where the day's first meeting happens, and almost nobody sees it. If you walked past, you would see a murder of crows in a tree by the water and one weathered street artist on a bench, paint on their hands and their jacket, feeding them. That is the whole meeting. That is exactly what it is supposed to look like.

The crows are reporting. All day yesterday they were out inspecting the city: roofs, wires, walls, parks, the edges where the streets meet the water. Now they are telling the artist, who is one of the Repair People, what they found. Which corners have gone quiet. Where a crack has opened. Where music and art and attention are running thin. The crows do not speak English, and they do not need to. The person on the bench understands without a word.

There is no chairperson, no agenda and no minutes. The meeting decides one thing: what the city needs today. Then the crows lift off, the artist picks up their bucket, and the water goes still. Somewhere behind them, without anyone noticing, the mist begins to move. If it looks like someone feeding crows, the meeting is probably going well.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
